deviceId.description: Supplied identifier of the device whose deletion was acknowledged.

tags.instructions: Find the device ID with `list-devices` and check `get-device` if ownership is uncertain. This deletes the device from the tailnet; no undo is provided by this tool. Use `deauthorize-device` to revoke approval without deleting the device, or `expire-device-key` to require reauthentication.

functions.name: delete-device-invite
functions.description: Delete one device-sharing invite. This acts on the invitation, not the shared device itself.

success.description: Tailscale acknowledged deletion of the invitation; this is not a device-deletion or accepted-share-revocation claim.

FunctionOutput_tailscale_deletedeviceinv.description: Acknowledgement that Tailscale deleted the invitation.

tags.instructions: Get deviceInviteId from `list-device-invites` or `get-device-invite`. Deletion removes the invitation; no restore action is documented. Do not use this to delete a device or assume it revokes access already established by an accepted share. Create a new invite if another invitation is needed.

functions.name: delete-device-posture-attribute

deviceId.description: Preferred device node ID or legacy device ID.

deviceId.description: Device identifier supplied for the completed deletion.

tags.instructions: Get device IDs from `list-devices` and exact custom: key spelling from `get-device-posture-attributes`. This removes only that attribute and its expiry, not the device or built-in node attributes. Use `upsert-device-posture-attribute` to assign a value again.

functions.name: delete-key
functions.description: Delete an auth key, API access token, OAuth client, or federated identity in the default tailnet, revoking its future use.

keyId.description: Opaque identifier of the key to delete, in the default tailnet; not its secret.

id.description: Identifier of the key targeted by the successful deletion.

deleted.description: True when Tailscale acknowledges deletion, not a claim that historical metadata is erased.

FunctionOutput_tailscale_deletekey.description: Acknowledgment of the requested key deletion.

It does not promise to remove devices previously enrolled with an auth key or revoke every derived token. Do not delete the credential needed by your own workflow unintentionally.

functions.name: delete-oauth-app
functions.description: Delete an OAuth app registration from a tailnet.

deleted.description: Provider acknowledged successful deletion; does not describe issued access-token validity.

FunctionOutput_tailscale_deleteoauthapp.description: Acknowledgement that Tailscale deleted the specified OAuth app registration.

tags.instructions: Get appId from `list-oauth-apps`. This deletes the app, not merely one scope grant. No restoration operation is provided; use `update-oauth-app` to change configuration instead.

functions.name: delete-posture-integration

FunctionOutput_tailscale_deleteposturein.description: Acknowledgement that Tailscale removed the posture integration configuration.

tags.instructions: Obtain postureIntegrationId from `list-posture-integrations` or `get-posture-integration`. This removes the integration configuration; no restore operation is documented. Existing posture data retention and downstream policy effects are not guaranteed by this tool. To integrate again, use `create-posture-integration` with the provider credentials.

deleted.description: Provider acknowledged deletion of the Service.

FunctionOutput_tailscale_deleteservice.description: Acknowledged deletion of the requested Service configuration.

tags.instructions: Get the Service name from `list-services`. This removes the Service resource, not its hosting devices. To revoke approval on only one host, use `update-service-host-approval`. No restoration workflow is provided.

functions.name: delete-tailnet
functions.description: Delete a tailnet together with all its users, devices, and configuration.

tailnetId.description: ID of the tailnet to delete; '-' selects the access token's default tailnet. Deletion includes all users, devices, and configuration.

FunctionInput_tailscale_deletetailnet.description: Explicit target for deletion of an entire tailnet.

tailnetId.description: Tailnet identifier submitted for deletion.

tags.instructions: This removes the entire tailnet, not just a device or setting. Obtain an explicit tailnet ID from `list-tailnets` or the admin console and ensure the connection can administer that tailnet. API-only tailnets require an appropriate tailnet-specific access token. No restoration workflow is provided.

functions.name: delete-user
functions.description: Delete a user from their tailnet. This is not suspension; this contract offers no recovery of the deleted user.

userId.description: Opaque identifier of the user to delete from their tailnet.
Identifier of the user whose deletion Tailscale acknowledged; not a restorable user snapshot.

FunctionOutput_tailscale_deleteuser.description: Acknowledgment of the requested tailnet user deletion.

tags.instructions: Get userId from `list-users` and inspect the user with `get-user` before deleting. This removes the user from their tailnet. For a reversible access interruption, use `suspend-user` instead; `restore-user` restores suspended access, not a documented deleted-user recovery. User-based tokens cannot delete their own user.

functions.name: delete-webhook
functions.description: Delete an existing webhook endpoint registration, removing its configuration for future event notifications. No restore operation is offered.

webhookId.description: Opaque ID of the existing webhook endpoint to delete, returned by list-webhooks.

FunctionInput_tailscale_deletewebhook.description: The existing webhook endpoint registration to delete.

webhookId.description: Identifier of the endpoint whose deletion Tailscale acknowledged.

FunctionOutput_tailscale_deletewebhook.description: Acknowledgment of the webhook endpoint deletion.

tags.instructions: Get webhookId from `list-webhooks`. Deletion removes that notification endpoint; no undo is provided. It does not delete the underlying users, devices or events. If you only need to check delivery configuration, use `get-webhook` or `test-webhook` instead. Already queued notification behavior is not guaranteed.

functions.name: enable-device-key-expiry
functions.description: Enable device key expiration at the original expiry time retained before expiration was disabled.

functions.name: expire-device-key

deviceId.description: Supplied device identifier whose key-expiration request was acknowledged.

FunctionOutput_tailscale_expiredevicekey.description: Acknowledgment of the device node-key expiration request.

tags.instructions: Use a device ID from `list-devices`. The device must belong to your tailnet. This requires reauthentication; it does not delete the device or merely toggle automatic expiry. Use `enable-device-key-expiry` or `disable-device-key-expiry` for the expiry setting.
